finite_assessment.complete_old_expression_basis: The entire old Ascension prayer already joins supplications, belief that the Savior shares the divine majesty, his abiding with us to the consummation of the age, and his own promise, in this sequence. The modern changes reorder the invocation, add a conventional graciousness qualifier and explicit pronouns, replace confidence with belief and a synonymous promise construction, and remove the seated predicate. The whole finite revised expression requires review; retaining common themes alone is not a sufficient basis. Old Ascension and modern Easter7 appointments are distinct.
exact_changes: Transpose Adesto, Domine, supplicationibus nostris to Supplicationibus nostris, Domine, adesto propitius, adding the adverb propitius.
Remove consedere, changing the explicit seated-with-you description to the retained with-you-in-your-majesty description. This predicate omission is substantive and explicitly disclosed.
Replace confidimus with credimus and move the verb between tua and maiestate.
Insert eum immediately after ita as the explicit subject of manere.
Replace quemadmodum est pollicitus with sicut ipse promisit: change the conjunction and synonymous promise verb while making the same subject explicit.

Replace the old Per. cue with the modern Qui tecum. long conclusion; its full words and separate Amen are independently old in Pustet1862AP88, and the exact secondary2002IGMR54 spells out the required modern form. No automatic truncation/expansion or exactoldwholebody identity is asserted.
finite_assessment.translation_notes: Adesto propitius is attend graciously; humani generis is human race; credimus is believe, without reintroducing the removed seated predicate. Sentiamus is experiential and rendered experience his remaining, preserving both the abiding and end-of-age limit. Ipse and the promise remain explicit. Full God/Spirit/eternal conclusion and distinct response are retained.
finite_assessment.strongest_contrary_argument: This prayer has several coordinated lexical, syntactic and predicate changes, not merely spelling or one-word correction. The removal of seated, invocation intensifier and explicit pronouns may constitute an editorial arrangement even though each clause has an old antecedent. A decision based solely on70percent coverage or common theological ideas would be invalid. The proposed finite assessment concerns this complete old two-clause supplication whose only actual narrative predicate change is removal of seated, with the same Savior, majesty, abiding, promise and time bound otherwise preserved. No general formula assembly or modern-prayer revision exemption is requested.
